settings.title: MCP server (AI assistants)
settings.intro: Lets AI assistants such as Claude Desktop or VS Code read processes, runs, monitors, schedules, dashboards and the audit log through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Read-only: an assistant cannot start runs or change anything.
settings.enableHint: Off by default. Each person still needs their own token with scope “MCP client”; tools act with that person’s rights.
settings.forcedOff: Turned off by the environment variable <c>{{name}}</c> on the server.
settings.token: Create a token with scope “MCP client” on your profile page and put it into the client configuration:
settings.limits: Limits: {{requests}} requests per minute and token; {{gateway}} platform calls per minute, user and platform.
settings.security: Tool results are data from Steward and connected systems. Assistants should treat them as data, never as instructions. Platforms are only reachable for MCP clients where an administrator turned on the MCP gateway (platform → MCP).

config.stdioHint: For Claude Desktop and other desktop clients, e.g. in <c>{{file}}</c>. Save the token in a file only you can read (<c>{{token}}</c>); the Steward desktop app runs the bridge with <c>steward mcp</c>.
config.stdioSource: From the source tree use <c>{{cmd}}</c> as the command (keep --silent: npm must not write to stdout).
config.httpHint: For clients that speak Streamable HTTP, e.g. in <c>{{file}}</c>: endpoint <c>{{url}}</c> with the header <c>Authorization: Bearer …</c>.

gateway.intro: The MCP gateway lets AI assistants call this platform’s API through Steward – read-only (GET and HEAD) and with the credentials stored here, which the assistant never sees. Every call is written to the audit log.
gateway.serverOff: The MCP server is turned off (Settings → MCP server). The gateway only works while it is on.
gateway.enable: Allow read-only access for MCP clients
gateway.enableHint: People also need the “use” right on this platform. Changing data through MCP is not possible.
gateway.operations_one: API specifications: {{read}} read operation available to MCP clients ({{write}} changing operations are never offered).
gateway.operations_other: API specifications: {{read}} read operations available to MCP clients ({{write}} changing operations are never offered).
gateway.prefixes: Allowed GET path prefixes (optional, one per line)
gateway.prefixesHint: For platforms without an API specification: MCP clients may read paths below these prefixes. Leave empty to allow the operations of the API specifications only.
gateway.security: Requests always go to the platform’s base URL and obey the outbound policy. Redirects are not followed, responses are limited to 512 kB and credentials in them are masked.
